summary: Chief Dawid Stuurman International Airport (PLZ) serves the coastal city of Gqeberha (formerly Port Elizabeth) in South Africa's Eastern Cape province, located approximately 7 km southwest of the city center. Originally known as Port Elizabeth International Airport, it was renamed in 2021 to honor Chief Dawid Stuurman, a 19th-century Xhosa leader and anti-colonial freedom fighter. The airport functions as the main gateway to the Nelson Mandela Bay metropolitan area and the broader Eastern Cape region, including popular destinations like Addo Elephant National Park and the Garden Route.
faqs:
Q: When was the airport renamed to Chief Dawid Stuurman International Airport?
A: The airport was officially renamed in early 2021 as part of South Africa's broader effort to restore indigenous names and honor historical figures, replacing the former Port Elizabeth International Airport designation.

Q: What airlines operate from PLZ?
A: The airport is primarily served by South African Airways, FlySafair, Airlink, and CemAir, offering domestic connections to Johannesburg, Cape Town, and Durban, along with select regional African routes.

Q: How far is the airport from central Gqeberha?
A: Chief Dawid Stuurman International Airport is approximately 7-10 km southwest of the city center, typically a 15-20 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Does the airport have international flights?
A: Yes, the airport handles a limited number of international flights, primarily to neighboring African countries, but it functions mainly as a domestic hub.
